The Axel Adler Scholarship is the University of Gothenburg's main scholarship for fee-paying students: a tuition-fee waiver for admitted bachelor's and master's students from outside the EU/EEA. It is named after the university's first vice-chancellor and awarded on academic merit — you must first be admitted to a programme before the scholarship round opens.

Programme Highlights

  • Tuition-fee waiver for the full duration of the admitted programme
  • Two-step process: admission first (15 January 2027 deadline), scholarship second (10 February – 8 March 2027 window)
  • Awarded on academic merit in the admission round — no separate essay in most years (confirm on the official page)
  • Fee-paying students from any country outside the EU/EEA (and Switzerland) are eligible

Who Should Apply

Non-EU/EEA students admitted to a bachelor's or master's programme at the University of Gothenburg starting autumn 2027 who are required to pay tuition. Only applicants who made the 15 January study-application deadline on universityadmissions.se can enter the scholarship round.

Funding and Costs

The scholarship removes the tuition fee (typically SEK 100,000–160,000 per year at Gothenburg) but pays no living stipend — budget around SEK 10,000–12,000/month for housing and living costs, and check the Swedish Migration Agency's maintenance requirement for the residence permit.

Deadline and How to Apply

Apply to your programme on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027, pay any application fee, and then submit the Axel Adler scholarship application in the university's scholarship portal during the 10 February – 8 March 2027 window. Key deadline information: study application 15 January 2027; scholarship application 10 February – 8 March 2027.

About University of Gothenburg

With roughly 37,000 students, the University of Gothenburg is one of Sweden's largest universities. The Axel Adler Scholarship is its principal tuition-fee waiver for fee-paying (non-EU/EEA) students admitted to bachelor's and master's programmes.

Official website: https://www.gu.se

Contact

Questions about this scholarship, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official scholarship page (see the Official Link section above). Always include your applicant ID or programme name so the admissions or scholarship team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements and deadlines on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form — transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
  • Deadlines shown in local time (CET/CEST) as published by the provider; convert to your own time zone before planning.
